page.layout: Full-width area at top: two engraved coin portraits side by side, with legends around their rims. Below them one text column, with two paragraphs and a closing line. No marginal notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Gathering signature at the foot right.

main_text.p: TVLLVS Hostilius tertius Romanorum Rex, regnauit anno mundi 3293. ante Christum natum 669.Hic primus Romanorum purpura & fascibus usus est: bella reparauit, fiducia bene exercitæ iuuentutis: Albanos vicit sexta congressione: Veientes, Sabinos, & Fidenates itidem. fœdere rupto,de Metio Suffetio supplicium sumit ob violatam fidem. Horatij Curiatios vincūt: Alba solo æquatur:ex Albanis & Romanis unus fit populus. Tradunt volentem Tullum Hostilium commentarios Numæ cùm quædam occulta solennia sacrificia Iouis Elicio facta inuenisset, operatum his sacris se abdidisse: sed non rite initum id sacrum esse: nec solùm nullam ei oblatam cœlestium speciem,sed ira Iouis solicitati praua religione, fulmine ipsum cum domo conflagrasse. Imperauit annos 32. ciuitatem auxit,adiecto Cœlio monte.hoc imperante Byzantium ciuitas condita est à Paufania Rege Spartanorum. Titus Liuius lib.1. Decad.1.Eutrop.lib.1.Diony.Halicarn.lib.3.

ANCVS Martius Numæ ex filia nepos, successit Tullo Hostilio anno mundi 3325. ante Christum natum 637. contra Latinos dimicauit,quos & vicit: Auentinum montem ciuitati adiecit,& Ianiculum.Pontem Subliciù in Tyberi fecit.Ostiam ciuitatem supra mare 16.miliario ab urbe Roma,condidit.Prol. lib.3.cap.1.& Strab.li.5. Huius temporibus Lucumo,cui nomen fuit L.Tarquinius Priscus,cum uxore Tanaquil Romam venit. Anno imperij 24. morbo perit Ancus , quo regnante Epidamnus est condita, quæ nunc Dyrrachium. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: The two coin engravings at the top carry legends around their rims, partly legible as TVLLVS HOSTIVS (right of left coin) and ANCVS MARTIVS (left of right coin); the rest of the legends is too worn to read and is not transcribed. Stray comma-like mark after "lib.3." at the right of the last line of the first paragraph is a printer's mark or speck, not text.
